name: hx_temperature_effectiveness_pntu
title: Heat exchangers: P-NTU temperature effectiveness (function library)
summary: Fifteen EES FUNCTIONs for the temperature effectiveness (P-NTU) method of a heat exchanger: the two common helper terms of the plate formulas, the temperature effectiveness P1 of the basic (counterflow, parallel, crossflow) arrangements, of the TEMA E, G, H and J shell-and-tube arrangements, of a finned-bundle air cooler and of a multipass plate heat exchanger, plus the inverse relations NTU1(P1, R1) (four closed forms and the equations of the numerical inversions, to be solved with NTU1 as an unknown).
language_features: IF/THEN/ELSE (nested, no ELSEIF: CoolSolve 0.3.0 ignores the ELSEIF condition)
DUPLICATE loops (nested, inside a FUNCTION body)
simultaneous equations for the implicit inversions (two equations for one variable)

authors: R. K. Shah and D. P. Sekulic (Fundamentals of Heat Exchanger Design)
W. Rohsenow, J. Hartnett and Y. Cho (Handbook of Heat Transfer)
S. G. Kandlikar and R. K. Shah (multipass plate effectiveness-NTU)
H. Schedwill and F. J. L. Nicole (air cooler arrangements)
origin.notes: ht 1.2.0, commit 85e0ee6 (2025-12-07), file ht/hx.py, functions P_NTU_Pp, P_NTU_Pc, temperature_effectiveness_air_cooler, temperature_effectiveness_basic, temperature_effectiveness_TEMA_E, temperature_effectiveness_TEMA_G, temperature_effectiveness_TEMA_H, temperature_effectiveness_TEMA_J, temperature_effectiveness_plate, NTU_from_P_basic, NTU_from_P_E, NTU_from_P_G, NTU_from_P_H, NTU_from_P_J and NTU_from_P_plate, MIT license, Copyright (C) 2016 Caleb Bell. The scientific basis of each relation is the original paper or book cited in its function comment block. Translation published under the CoolSolve_Library MIT license (decision D3).

verification.reference: doctest values of ht 1.2.0 ht/hx.py (case A: R1 = 1/3, NTU1 = 1 for the TEMA and plate relations, R1 = 0.1 and NTU1 = 4 for the basic counterflow relation, R1 = 0.5, NTU1 = 2 with 2 rows and 2 passes for the air cooler, x = 5 with y = 0.4 and y = 0.7 for the two helper terms) plus values computed with the same ht functions (case B: the steam/oil crossflow rating of the ht docstring, stream 1 = the process stream, R1 = 0.14242, NTU1 = 2.16007; one call per remaining branch); 81 output values in total
verification.notes: compare_solution.py: 81 common variables, 0 differ (rtol=0.001). The largest relative deviation, 8.3e-8, is on temperature_effectiveness_basic_extra4, the exact crossflow arrangement evaluated by the composite Simpson quadrature (80 intervals) of the integrand inside the function, which CoolSolve cannot evaluate there; the same quadrature in the main program of CSL-0090 gives 1.4e-8. Over the other 80 values the largest deviation is 1.2e-9, on NTU_from_P_G_A (convergence tolerance of the implicit inversion); the other 79 agree to 6.6e-10, i.e. round-off.
